findings_addressed: FIX-1 [P2] 1/3 — `setup.cfg` missing from the manifest oracle (conftest.py:39-51). The design's recognized-manifest table listed `setup.cfg`; `tracked_manifest_paths()` did not, so a tracked `setup.cfg` added later is silently missed while AC-SBOM-03 still passes — the design stated a requirement the tests did not enforce. CLOSED: `setup.cfg` added to MANIFEST_BASENAMES, and rather than patching the one name the ENTIRE recognized table was re-diffed against the helper — `poetry.lock`, `Pipfile`, `yarn.lock` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` were confirmed already present on both sides. The tuple is now split into 'matches tracked paths today' / 'recognized, forward-looking' with an explicit lockstep warning, and design §5.1 was promoted from a prose list to the same two-group table. Verified none of the five forward-looking names is tracked at cbb56212 (`git ls-files | grep -E '(^|/)(setup\.cfg|Pipfile|poetry\.lock|yarn\.lock|pnpm-lock\.yaml)$'` exits 1 with no output), so §5.1's 28-path enumeration is unchanged.

FIX-1 [P2] 2/3 — no `purl` assertion (test_cyclonedx.py:32-35). REQ-6 requires a purl per component and §5.5 makes the purl the bom-ref — the component identity an advisory feed matches a locked version against — but CycloneDX 1.6 accepts `name` + `version` alone, so a purl-less document passed AC-SBOM-10. CLOSED: AC-SBOM-10 now asserts per component that `purl` is present, carries an ecosystem prefix in {pkg:cargo/, pkg:npm/, pkg:pypi/}, EQUALS the `bom-ref`, and (for resolved components) has an `@version` segment equal to the component's own version; plus a document-level assertion that the purl-type set is EXACTLY {cargo, npm, pypi} — this repo tracks manifests in all three, so a missing type means an entire ecosystem was dropped and a fourth type means something leaked in. Test renamed test_cyclonedx_document_is_schema_valid_and_purl_identified; §4's AC table and §5.5 restate the contract.

FIX-1 [P2] 3/3 — dependency-graph coverage was vacuous (test_cyclonedx.py:91-98). `doc.get("dependencies", [])` tolerates an EMPTY array, which is trivially 'closed', and the only depth assertion required a `direct` component — so an implementation emitting the manifest-derived direct set with ZERO lockfile-derived library<->library edges passed, i.e. REQ-8 was unenforced and the core reason the tool exists went ungated. CLOSED: AC-SBOM-12 now asserts the array is non-empty; the graph is closed in BOTH directions (every declared component has a `ref` entry, leaves carrying an empty `dependsOn` — direction 1 alone is what an empty array satisfies); at least one edge originates at a library rather than the metadata root component; and at least one KNOWN LOCKFILE-ONLY crate arrives tagged `transitive`. The sentinel set is proc-macro2 / quote / syn / unicode-ident / serde_derive, each present in the tracked Cargo.lock and declared by NO dependency table of any tracked non-excluded Cargo.toml at cbb56212 (378 of the 410 locked crates are in that position, computed from the tree), so they can only reach the BOM by walking the lock's edges. Only ONE survivor is required, which is the deliberate drift allowance; §5.5 records the caveat and the test says so in its failure message.

FIX-1 STEER 1 — .github/dependabot.yml is an existing tracked source of record for the tiering, and the first pass never cited it. §5.3 now derives the tier rules from it entry by entry (pip /src/python -> shipped, cargo / -> shipped incl. all src/rust/crates/* members, npm /src/ts -> shipped, npm / -> dev-tooling per the R-DEP-2 note, github-actions / -> out of BOM scope and recorded as deliberate) together with its explicit 'Deliberately NOT covered (do NOT add ...)' list (/python as the uv-managed EVAL ENV and 'the source of the idna/torch security-alert noise'; dev/research/** and data/corpus-data/** requirements files; dev/release/fixtures/cargo-skew/**). Consequence (a): §5.2 now records that the fixture exclusion is the ALREADY-RULED position — on disk since 0.8.11.1 / R-SW-5, for the same stated reason (noise/orphans) — which is considerably stronger than a fresh carve-out; pip-skew is unnamed there only because no pip directory was ever configured near it, and it takes the identical rule. Consequence (b): dev/tools/mermaid/package.json is a REAL tracked npm manifest covered by NO configured Dependabot directory (the npm entries are /src/ts and / only) — a genuine coverage gap of the same class as the R-DEP-2 note, which records that the root package-lock.json carried two live advisories (markdown-it GHSA-6v5v-wf23-fmfq, js-yaml GHSA-h67p-54hq-rp68) while under no directory so its security PRs never auto-opened. 0.8.20 rules NOTHING about it — .github/** is out of bounds for every leg — but the tool surfaces it mechanically as a set-difference over its own discovery output, which is a cashable demonstration of value given that LIBRARY-BUMP-STEWARD.md's own DoD includes 'dependabot.yml reconciled' (now cited in §1). Handed to Slice 33 §4 / 0.8.22.

FIX-1 STEER 2 — findings home weighed against all three conventions; RULING CHANGED. §5.6 was rewritten as a three-way comparison and the home moved from dev/design/0.8.20-slice-33-library-sweep-3-findings.md to dev/plans/runs/0.8.20-slice-33-library-sweep-3-FINDINGS.md. Basis: (a) dev/plans/runs/<version>-<slug>-FINDINGS.md is the dominant house convention for a DATED RUN REPORT (0.8.2-m1-FINDINGS.md, 0.8.3-rerank-tune-FINDINGS.md, 0.8.4-cost-probe-FINDINGS.md, IR-C-retrieval-findings.md), dev/plans/README.md scopes runs/ to 'slice logs, reviewer notes, and status boards' and dev/plans/ to 'release execution planning + run artifacts', and the slice's own -output.json already lands there under the house split (durable .md + -output.json tracked, raw logs gitignored by per-run glob). (b) dev/design/ is the weakest of the three on its OWN README's terms ('keep here: engine, retrieval, scheduler, vector, recovery, release design docs / cross-cutting design constraints') — a survey of ~400 third-party versions is neither — and the dev/design/0.8.20-sqlite-vec-99-vec0-delete-probe.md precedent is off-point, because that probe was commissioned to settle a DESIGN question so its output WAS a design constraint, whereas this one settles nothing about FathomDB's design and feeds 0.8.22's backlog. (c) dev/deps/ stays the home for PER-DEPENDENCY DOSSIERS, which Slice 33 mints none of (ASCERTAIN, NEVER IMPLEMENT), and its README explicitly forbids 'generated audit output dumps with no summary'. Division of labour recorded in §5.6: dev/plans/runs/ holds run-level findings, dev/deps/ holds per-dependency dossiers, and a later sweep that re-reviews a dependency writes dev/deps/<dep>.md citing the run report by path. Cost acknowledged honestly: lint-design-status.sh's frontmatter gate does not reach dev/plans/runs/** (nor does lint-plans-status.sh, which is top-level dev/plans/*.md only); this is consistent rather than a regression, since NO existing runs/ findings doc carries frontmatter, so the fixed doc shape adopts the H1 + bolded provenance line convention instead of importing a gate that would not fire. AC-SBOM-18's expected SLICE_33_FINDINGS_DOC moved with the ruling and the new path was verified NOT gitignored (`git check-ignore -v` exits 1).
